label: Combinatorial logical space at a world, and elementary existence
definition: LogicalSpaceAt F V w is Saturates F V w with the valuation as report map: for every assignment s : A -> Prop of truth values to the atoms, some world v accessible from w in F has exactly that atomic profile (V v = s). The atoms then vary jointly and freely over the worlds accessible from w: every combination of obtaining and not obtaining of the atomic states of affairs is a possible world from w. OnlyLogicalNecessityAt F V w means every box-free formula boxed at w is a NECESSARY_16 tautology. ElementaryExistenceAt o w is LogicalSpaceAt for the route frame o.frame and the existence valuation of o (the atom of a candidate holds at v exactly when it exists at v): every combination of existence and non-existence of the candidates is realized at an accessible world. NotElementaryExistenceAt is its negation.
note: Analyst formulation, attribution deferred; Tractatus 1.13, 2.04-2.063, 4.211, 5.134 (logical space, independence of states of affairs) are navigation only. Not a causal, grounding or explanatory relation and not a claim that any actual atoms are elementary: which propositions are elementary, and which assignments are admitted as genuinely possible, stays OPEN. Saturation is joint realization, not probabilistic independence (AtomismIndependence, #1088). Structural consequences proved in the batch: in logical space a box-free formula is boxed exactly when it is a tautology; any box-free formula that is an exact existence dictionary for a box-existent bearer is a tautology; the universal frame on all assignments is S5. ElementaryExistenceAt applies the same notion to the existence facts of the candidates; it is the precise extra premise a 'there is only logical necessity' thesis needs to bear on de re box-existence, and the box K necessary-being node excludes it at the same world. Distinguished from the S5 frame premise (a frame law, no claim about which valuations are realized) and from contingency of one being (one missing combination suffices for that, not all combinations).
